name: com.regimecard/market-regime
title: Regime Card
description: Market regime: US risk-on or risk-off? Live score, stress gate. USDC on Base, Polygon, Solana.

tools.name: sample_reading
tools.description: What was the US market regime at the last close? Returns the newest settled Regime Card reading, the same one regimecard.com shows: a percentile from 0 to 100, one of five regimes, the eight cross-asset category labels, and the paid routes with their prices. Free. One reading per US trading day, settled at 4:30 PM ET. Useful as a free first look at the response shape and the paid routes.

tools.name: live_reading
tools.description: Is the US market risk-on or risk-off right now? Returns the live Regime Card reading: a percentile from 0 (most risk-off) to 100 (most risk-on) and one of five market regimes, from Risk-Off to Risk-On, built from eight cross-asset signals, beside the last settled close. $0.01 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Updates about once an hour while the US market is open, from a little after 10 AM ET. Marked "live" until it settles at 4:30 PM ET; otherwise the last settled reading. Useful when an agent needs a market sentiment or market conditions check for today, or a fear and greed alternative that reads credit, volatility, rates, currencies, commodities and sectors.

tools.name: stress_gate
tools.description: Is market stress calm, elevated or stressed right now? Returns the Regime Card stress gate: the overall state (Calm, Elevated or Stressed), how many of its three components are confirmed (N of 3), and each one's state (Credit, Volatility, Rates: Clear or Confirmed). A credit stress and volatility regime check. $0.01 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Updates about once an hour while the US market is open, the first a little after 10 AM ET; marked "settled" outside market hours.

tools.name: lookup_symbols
tools.description: How has this stock or crypto typically done in markets like today's? Returns, for one stock or crypto symbol per call (any US stock, plus the covered crypto list), its typical return and how often it rose over 1 to 12 months from the current regime. Stocks add sensitivity versus the S&P 500 and up to 5 peer symbols. A symbol with no price data is free. $0.01 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Settled figures, updated after each US close (coins daily). The same figures as the symbol's page on regimecard.com. Useful when an agent needs a stock lookup: stock data, stock returns by market regime or crypto returns by market regime.

symbol.description: One stock or crypto symbol: any US stock, or a coin on the covered crypto list, for example "NVDA" or "BTC". Upper or lower case. One symbol per call.

symbols.description: The earlier form of the same input: a list with exactly one stock or crypto symbol, for example ["NVDA"].

items.description: One stock, ETF or crypto symbol.

inputSchema.description: A JSON object with exactly one field: symbol, or the earlier symbols with one entry. One symbol per call. A second symbol is a second call.

tools.name: lookup_batch
tools.description: How have the stocks and coins in this portfolio typically done in markets like today's? Returns a batch stock lookup: for up to 100 stock or crypto symbols in one request and one payment, each one's typical return and how often it rose over 1 to 12 months from the current regime. Symbols without a regimecard.com page are listed, not charged. $0.01 per covered symbol in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Settled figures, updated after each US close (coins daily). The exact total for a request is stated before any payment. Useful when an agent needs a portfolio check, a watchlist scan or stock data in bulk by market regime.

symbols.description: Up to 100 stock or crypto symbols, any case.

tools.name: crypto_regime
tools.description: Is crypto risk-on or risk-off, and what does bitcoin risk look like in markets like today's? Returns the current crypto market regime and each covered coin's typical return and how often it rose over 1, 2 and 3 months when the period started in this regime, as historical odds. $0.01 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Regime updates after each US close, coins once a day. Useful when an agent needs the market regime for crypto across BTC and altcoins. Covers altcoin risk as well as bitcoin.

tools.name: brief
tools.description: What is the stock market today, in one call? Returns the live market regime reading, the stress gate, and the scorecard row for the regime of the last settled close: what the S&P 500 did in the 5 and 20 trading days after past readings in that regime (typical return, how often it rose, a bad outcome as a drawdown risk measure). A cross-asset macro signal. $0.03 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Updates about once an hour while the US market is open, the first a little after 10 AM ET. The reading settles at 4:30 PM ET; the scorecard row follows the last settled close. Useful when an agent wants one reading as a risk check before a trade or as a position sizing input.

tools.name: sector_leaders
tools.description: Which sectors and stocks have done best and worst in markets like today's? Returns the ten sectors of the regimecard.com stocks page ranked by their stocks' median typical return over 1, 2 or 3 months from the current regime, each with its five highest and five lowest. With one sector named, every stock in it, ranked. It covers the stocks with Regime Card pages. Any other US stock can be checked one at a time with /v1/lookup. $0.05 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). One sector: $0.03 per call. Settled figures, updated after each US close: the ones the stock pages on regimecard.com print. Useful when an agent needs sector rotation context for the current market regime.

sector.description: One sector: all its covered stocks, ranked, at the one-sector price. Without it, every sector.

inputSchema.description: Query parameters, all optional. Any other value is a free 400.

tools.name: scorecard
tools.description: What has the S&P 500 done after past readings in this regime? Returns the scorecard row for the regime of the last settled close, as regimecard.com publishes it on its history page: the S&P 500's typical return and how often it rose in the 5 and 20 trading days after past readings in that regime, and a bad outcome as a downside measure. Any of the five regimes can be asked for by key. $0.01 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Updated after each US close. The row follows the last settled close, whose date is asOf. Useful when an agent needs base rates for the S&P 500 in the current market regime.

regime.description: One of the five regimes, by its key. Without it, the regime of the last settled close.

inputSchema.description: Query parameters, all optional. Any other value is a free 400.

tools.name: earnings_drift
tools.description: Which stocks are drifting after earnings right now? Returns the Regime Card post-earnings drift (PEAD) tracker: large US stocks that reported earnings in about the last two weeks, in the tracker's own order, each with its report date, its earnings surprise, its first-session reaction and its price drift since the report. $0.02 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). Rescanned each morning before the US open; prices refresh in rotation while the US market is open. "stale" is true until the current session's rescan has completed. Useful when an agent needs an earnings surprise check, post-earnings announcement drift data or an earnings calendar follow-up for stocks.

tools.name: conditions_gate
tools.description: What are US market conditions right now, in one small call? Returns the current Regime Card regime (Risk-On to Risk-Off) and the stress gate's overall state (Calm, Elevated or Stressed) with how many of its three components are confirmed (N of 3). Conditions only: no percentile, no per-component detail, no history. $0.002 per call in USDC on Base, Polygon or Solana (x402). The regime and the stress gate each update about once an hour while the US market is open, the first a little after 10 AM ET. The top-level asOf and status are the regime's; the stress gate carries its own. Useful when an agent checks market conditions before every action and needs the smallest answer at the lowest price.
